design_contract.pipeline: register -> active invariant relation identification -> residual bridge only if needed -> common executor composition

stochastic_neural_aggregate.notes: Each seed trains independent candidate and held-out target MLP/GRU specialists with independent private input/output permutations. Runtime relation observations are actual multinomial samples; registry relation probabilities are estimated from repeated candidate samples.

facts: The same core.py ran discrete finite-state, continuous scalar, and stochastic neural environments without operation names or environment cardinality in the core.
Discrete: 60/60 routes, wrong 0, unresolved 0; 50/50 depth1-5 programs.
Continuous: 60/60 routes, wrong 0, unresolved 0; 50/50 depth1-5 programs.
Stochastic neural seeds15-17 aggregate: 96/96 routes, wrong 0, unresolved 0; 150/150 depth1-5 programs; mean relation queries ~2.99.
For deliberately exact relation-equivalent pairs, relation-only identification returned UNRESOLVED 80/80 total across discrete+continuous; adding one grounded bridge resolved 80/80 with wrong 0.
boundaries: This V2 screen still assumes a shared semantic intervention/probe domain at the environment wrapper boundary.
Registered execute_common adapters are supplied by each environment; neural output-token inverse maps are currently known inside the wrapper rather than discovered by V2.
Composition is hard source selection followed by common-interface execution; sparse probability fusion is not yet reintroduced.
The neural models are small synthetic MLP/GRU specialists, not unrelated pretrained models.
Open-world gauge-family misspecification and persistent instance uncertainty are not yet wired into this clean-room core.
